**Issue #4246 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #4246: Patch: screen the reply's switched-off combined lethal again and switch it on if the screen keeps it
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the computer opponent imagines your next turn, it currently scores its attacks one hit at a time. So it can misevaluate a board where two attackers only win the game together: it sees a mere kill, spends an attacker removing a unit, and misses that sending both at your hero would end the game. Since the newest change it can also do the reverse: hide a unit in Defense and watch its own imagined combined lethal evaporate. A built-in alternative already exists that counts all remaining attacks together and sends them at the hero first when they reach past the blockers. It is switched off because a single measurement on 2026-11-01 came out flat (203-197 on 400 games, edge +0.015 with an interval crossing zero). This re-runs that measurement on today's opponent model and flips the switch only if the new measurement says the alternative plays better. Players notice slightly sharper computer attacks and blocks; nothing else changes.

## Why

- The design already invites this: SPEC 9.9's opponent's-reply paragraph describes the combined-lethal reply and says it is switched off (`AI_REPLY.open_lethal`) until a screen keeps it.
- The 2026-11-01 screen predates five changes to the reply: combined damage-pool and conversion reads (R4064000/R4064001), Burn/Toxic and exile blow pricing (R4065000/R4065001), per-attack combat math with First-Strike-stopped blows worth nothing (R4171000), and the new Defense-switch wall logic (R4187000). The old reading measured a different reply.
- R4187000's own ruling note documents a concrete mis-evaluation under the current setting: with the switch off, the reply's attack is one hit, a wall beats it on the evaluation's flat lethal-threat cliff, and with two 4/4s against the seat at 8 the opponent walls and misses its own combined lethal. The switch is exactly the guard that case wants: with it on, attacks that together reach the hero count as the win, so the attack wins the comparison and the lethal is taken.
- Nothing open or recently closed covers this: #1283 (lethal against every trap) is the solver's hidden-card coverage, a different mechanism, and #3823 (ranking the AI's own prompt answers) stays untouched.

## Proposal

1. Build a candidate with `open_lethal: true` and nothing else changed.
2. Predeclare the screen size (400 improve-dev games is the floor; 800 if the expected gain is a point or two), then run the arena screen from training/improve.md (`arena --set improve-dev`, candidate as self against a control built from the committed tip). Trace losses with `cargo jackioh trace`. Never screen on gate deals, which stay hold-out.
3. Keep the flip only if the paired edge's low end is above zero; otherwise revert and record the numbers on the issue. No extending a close screen and no second run for a better read, per the screen rules.
4. The existing `open_lethal_1634` tests already thread both settings through `simulate_reply_with` and assert the shipped behavior follows the constant, so the flip is test-held by construction; add a `run_puzzle` case in that module only if a trace finds a new concrete position.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (`AI_REPLY.open_lethal` and its screen comment)
- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` (no change expected; `simulate_reply_with` already threads the flag)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs` (`open_lethal_1634` module, only if a trace finds a new puzzle)
- `spec/09-architecture.md`, 9.9 opponent's-reply paragraph (the until-a-screen-keeps-it sentence, updated to the outcome)
- Procedure followed: `training/improve.md`, A screen

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Screen size predeclared on the issue before it starts; control built from the committed tip.
- [ ] Arena tally reported with wins and paired edge plus 95 percent interval; kept only if the low end is above zero, else reverted with numbers recorded.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` green and `cargo jackioh spec check` green.
- [ ] No gate-deal seeds used in any screen.
- [ ] The spec sentence matches the shipped value.

## Size and risks

Small code change (one constant, its comment, one spec sentence), hard measurement: 400-800 arena games of compute, roughly an hour on a runner. Difficulty is hard by the AI convention. The main risk is the appearance of re-rolling one switch until it turns green; it is contained by the changed conditions (five reply changes plus a newly documented bad interaction), a predeclared size, and keep-only-above-zero with no extensions. If the retire-the-learned-evaluation proposal lands first this is unaffected (reply ranking, not evaluation). No hidden-information change: the flag only re-ranks attacks on the same sampled worlds.

     - skip the screen;

5. **Run the screen once.** Run it as one background Bash command (`run_in_background: true`, `timeout: 7200000`):

   ```sh

   ```

   - **Expected time.** About 96 minutes. The planner timed 16 paired games, self against a copy of the tip's build on a private base, at 115 s on this 4-core runner.
   - **Nothing else CPU-heavy meanwhile.** No cargo, no pnpm, no subagents while it runs: they slow the screen. Reading, and drafting the step 6 and 7 text in `.bot-notes.md`, is fine.
   - **No output until the end.** The arena prints only once every game is done (`play_games` collects them all), so it cannot be stopped early or read early.
   - **If the session is cut off before the tally prints.** Nothing was read, so the next run starts this same 800-game command again from step 2. Say so in `.bot-notes.md` before the command starts.

   When it ends:
   - Take the tally with `grep '^{"a":"self"' /tmp/screen-4246.log`. Check that `games` is 800 and `deals` is 400.
   - Count faulted games with `grep -c '"simPanics":[1-9]\|"fallbacks":[1-9]' /tmp/screen-4246.log`.
   - **Write the whole tally line into `.bot-notes.md` `## State` at once**, before any other step, so a cut-off run never screens again.

6. **Decide, and write the comment.** Kept means the printed `edgeLow` is greater than `0.0`. A printed `0.0` or below is not kept. Do not extend, re-run or round the result.

   Fill the placeholders from the tally: `<A>` is `aWins`, `<B>` is `bWins`, then `edge`, `edgeLow`, `edgeHigh`, and `<control>` is the step 2 hash. If `draws` or `aborted` is above 0, add "with <n> drawn" or "<n> aborted" after the games, as the `#1696` comment does. Write no date. Keep every line at or under 110 columns.

   **If kept,** leave `open_lethal: true` and replace the two `// #1634:` comment lines with:

   ```rust
       // #1634, #4246: on. #1634's screen read 203-197, edge 0.015 (-0.002 to 0.032), which kept nothing;
       // #4246's, on the reply as it stands since, read <A>-<B> on 800 games, edge <edge> (<edgeLow> to
       // <edgeHigh>), against the control <control> (training/improve.md, A screen).
   ```

   **If not kept,** set the value back to `open_lethal: false` and replace the comment with:

   ```rust
       // #1634: off. On, its screen read 203-197, edge 0.015 (-0.002 to 0.032), and #4246's, on the reply as
       // it stands since, read <A>-<B> on 800 games, edge <edge> (<edgeLow> to <edgeHigh>), against the
       // control <control>; neither keeps it (training/improve.md, A screen).
   ```

   Then skip step 7.

7. **Kept only: update the text that describes the switch.**
   - `spec/09-architecture.md`, line 167: replace `This is switched off (`AI_REPLY.open_lethal`) until a screen keeps it.` with `It is switched on (`AI_REPLY.open_lethal`), kept by issue #4246's screen.`
   - `docs/polish/3-ai.md`, line 727: replace `switched off until a screen keeps` with `switched on once #4246's screen kept`. Line 728 begins `it);` and stays as it is.
   - `spec/rulings/R4187000.md`, line 19: replace `` `AI_REPLY.open_lethal` is off, `` with `` `AI_REPLY.open_lethal` was off then, ``. Leave the rest of the bullet alone: the guard it explains still applies with the switch on.

8. **Run the checks** in this order, after the screen:
   1. `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`
   2. `cargo fmt --check`
   3. `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`
   4. `cargo jackioh spec check`
   5. `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`. It should report kind AI and need no fragment; earlier AI pull requests carried none.
   6. **Kept only:** `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/tutorial src/practice src/routes/practice`. These are the tests outside `crates/ai` that play the shipped AI on fixed seeds (`training/improve.md`, Beyond the gate). The harness's `--changed` web run does not reach them; CI's web job does.

   If kept and a lesson or practice test fails because of the flip, do not edit the test. Then:
   - set `open_lethal` back to `false` with the step 6 "not kept" comment, adding after its numbers: `, though it kept, <test file> failed with it on`;
   - undo step 7;
   - report the failure for a person to decide on.

9. **Write the final report.** It contains:
   - the size (800, predeclared in this plan);
   - the control's hash;
   - the full tally JSON line;
   - the faulted-game count;
   - kept or reverted;
   - every check above with its result.

   Say that no trace was run and no puzzle added, and why (Departures).

## Tests

- `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs` has two tests in `open_lethal_1634` that follow `AI_REPLY.open_lethal`, so they hold whichever value ships:
  - `b41_takes_a_lethal_that_needs_both_attacks_over_a_kill_worth_more_than_one_hit` (asserts `shipped.result.is_some() == AI_REPLY.open_lethal`);
  - `decide_blocks_one_of_two_attackers_that_are_lethal_only_together` (asserts `survives == AI_REPLY.open_lethal`).

  Command: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai open_lethal_1634`.
- The `r4187000_*` tests in the same file must stay green with the flip: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai r4187000`.
- Whole crate: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`. It ran green on the tip in 5m01s: 958, 95 and 57 tests in its three test binaries.
- No new test. The flip is held by the tests above; see Departures for why there is no trace and no puzzle.

## Done when

- [ ] The control was built from the unedited HEAD, and its hash is recorded.
- [ ] Exactly one screen ran: 800 games, `--set improve-dev`, never a gate base. Its full tally is in `.bot-notes.md` and in the report.
- [ ] `open_lethal` is `true` only if `edgeLow` > 0, else `false`. The comment carries both screens' numbers.
- [ ] If kept: the §9.9 sentence, `docs/polish/3-ai.md` and R4187000's bullet say it is on. If not: none of the three changed.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, fmt, clippy, spec check and classify are green; if kept, the lesson and practice tests are green too.

## Risks

- **Time.**
  - The builder's model call may run 150 minutes (`call_timeout_minutes`), and the screen takes about 96 of them. Steps 2-4 take about 10 minutes before it and step 8 about 15 after, so start the screen as soon as step 4 is green.
  - If the call is cut off mid-screen, the next run repeats it once, from scratch (step 5).
  - If the tally was already read, the next run must use the recorded tally and must not screen again.
- **Fishing for a result.** Pairing and the predeclared 800 contain it, as do one run, keep only above 0, and no rounding or extension.
- **Effects outside `crates/ai`.** CI runs the web and e2e smoke jobs on a `crates/ai/src` change (`scripts/ci-scope.sh`). e2e spec 13 needs an Easy game to last four turns; the flip only changes how the AI imagines its opponent's attacks. A later fix run that finds a test outside `crates/ai` failing because of the flip follows this rule:
  - if the test pins an incidental outcome of an AI game (a hash, a record), update it with a `#4246` comment;
  - if it checks a property (a lesson that must be winnable, a turn floor), revert the switch as in step 8.
- **Determinism and hidden information.** Both are unchanged. The flag re-ranks attacks on the same sampled worlds through `ready_gap` on the determinized state, and adds no randomness or reads.

**Departures from muse's plan:**
- The size is fixed here at 800, and this plan is the predeclaration. The builder cannot post an issue comment.
- `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/jackioh` replaces `target/release/jackioh`.
- The trace step is dropped. `cargo jackioh trace` replays only gate matchups from the tuning series (`crates/tools/src/trace.rs` header), not arena dev-set games, so it cannot trace the screen's losses, and the issue adds a puzzle only if a trace finds one.
- On a keep, `docs/polish/3-ai.md` and R4187000's stale "is off" are fixed. #1683 and #4210 both edited that doc, and a doc that contradicts the spec is a bug (CLAUDE.md).
- The comment is rewritten in both outcomes, as the in-tree record.

## Open questions

None for the build. If the screen keeps the switch but a lesson test fails with it on, step 8 reverts it and a person decides whether to fix the lesson and turn the switch on.
````
